subject: general
question: If sin x = (1)/(sqrt{10)}, then find sec x in simplest form.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given, sin x = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse = 1 / √10

Base = √(H² − P²) = √(10 − 1) = √9 = 3

We know, sec x = Hypotenuse / Base

⇒ sec x = √10 / 3

**∴ The correct answer is √10/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sin x = 1 / √10

**Formula Used:**

sin x = Perpendicular (P) / Hypotenuse (H)

sec x = Hypotenuse (H) / Base (B)

H² = P² + B²

 
 
 
 x Base (B) = 3 Perpendicular (P) = 1 Hypotenuse (H) = √10 

**Calculations:**

⇒ By comparing, Perpendicular (P) = 1 and Hypotenuse (H) = √10

⇒ According to Pythagoras theorem: (√10)² = 1² + B²

⇒ 10 = 1 + B²

⇒ B² = 9

⇒ Base (B) = 3

Now, substitute the values into the formula for sec x:

⇒ sec x = H / B

⇒ sec x = √10 / 3

**∴ The correct answer is √10/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

For a right-angled triangle, sin θ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse, cos θ = Base / Hypotenuse, and tan θ = Perpendicular / Base.

Pythagorean Identities

The primary Pythagorean identity is sin² θ + cos² θ = 1. Other forms include 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ and 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ.

Reciprocal Identities

The reciprocal of cos θ is sec θ (sec θ = 1 / cos θ). Similarly, cosec θ = 1 / sin θ and cot θ = 1 / tan θ.
